```{r config}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CONFIGURATION — edit this section for a new study
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

cfg <- list(

  # ── Input / output paths ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Folder containing the .nd2 files (flat folder, not recursive)
  input_dir  = here("../JP20260213/"),

  # Where composite TIFFs + slide PNGs are written
  output_dir = here("output/"),

  # Path to the ND2 -> composite TIFF python script
  py_script  = here("nd2_composite/nd2_composite.py"),

  # ── Filename parsing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ND2 filename (without extension) is split on this delimiter...
  filename_delim = "_",

  # ...then matched against this regex. Edit the named groups if your
  # naming convention changes — the rest of the document only refers to
  # these group names, not their position, so reordering fields here is
  # enough to adapt to a new format.
  #
  # Default format: date_Study_Type_Batch_Sample_Zinfo
  #   e.g. 20260213_ZDNA_Optimisations_OP2_BiofilmNo1_Z1
  #   e.g. 20260213_ZDNA_Optimisations_OP2_BiofilmNo1_Z1x40
  #   e.g. 20260213_ZDNA_Optimisations_OP2_BiofilmAllH_S3
  #
  # "biofilmNo" captures whatever sample label sits in that field
  # position (BiofilmNo1, BiofilmAllH, S3, ...) — it no longer requires
  # the literal word "Biofilm" or a trailing number. It only needs to
  # be unique per sample so slides group correctly. The trailing
  # "_Zinfo" segment is entirely optional, so filenames with no Z/zoom
  # info at all still parse (z and zoom come back as NA).
  #
  # Required named groups: biofilmNo, z, zoom (z and zoom may be NA)
  # NOTE: ICU regex (used by stringr/stringi) requires capture-group names
  # to be alphanumeric only — no underscores. Group names below are
  # deliberately camelCase for this reason.
  filename_pattern = paste0(
    "^(?<date>[0-9]{6,8})_",
    "(?<study>[^_]+)_",
    "(?<type>[^_]+)_",
    "(?<batch>[^_]+)_",
    "(?<biofilmNo>[^_]+?)",
    "(_Z(?<z>[0-9]+)(x(?<zoom>[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?))?)?$"
  ),

  # Files whose stem matches this regex are excluded before parsing —
  # e.g. single-image files (no Z-stack) marked with a trailing "_S<n>",
  # which this pipeline can't turn into a MIP composite. Set to NULL to
  # disable exclusion filtering entirely.
  exclude_pattern = "_S[0-9]+$",

  # ── nd2_composite.py arguments ───────────────────────────────────────
  # Extra flags passed to every nd2_composite.py call. Edit freely
  # (e.g. add "--scale-bar", "--channel-labels", change --suffix).
  py_extra_args = c("--suffix", "_comp", "--lut-min", "0", "--lut-max", "4095"),
  py_suffix     = "_comp",   # must match the --suffix value above

  # Python packages this pipeline needs. reticulate::py_require()
  # provisions an isolated environment automatically (via uv) so no
  # manual venv/conda setup is required on any machine running this doc.
  # "python-pptx" builds the final slide deck with precisely positioned
  # images and captions (needed because pandoc's markdown->pptx path
  # cannot reliably place multiple images side-by-side, or place any
  # image inside a table cell).
  py_packages = c("nd2", "tifffile", "numpy", "tqdm", "Pillow", "python-pptx"),

  # ── Slide layout ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  slide_image_width_in = 3.0,   # width per image, side-by-side layout
  max_images_per_row    = 3,

  # Output pptx path
  pptx_path = here("Microscopy Report.pptx"),

  # PowerPoint slide size (widescreen default)
  slide_width_in  = 13.333,
  slide_height_in = 7.5,

  # Set TRUE to re-run nd2_composite.py even if a composite TIFF already
  # exists for a given source file (useful after changing LUT/contrast
  # settings). FALSE reuses existing outputs and is much faster.
  force_reconvert = TRUE
)
```

```{r derive-paths}
dir.create(cfg$output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
tiff_dir <- file.path(cfg$output_dir, "tiff")
png_dir  <- file.path(cfg$output_dir, "png")
dir.create(tiff_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(png_dir,  recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r discover-files}
nd2_files <- list.files(cfg$input_dir, pattern = "\\.nd2$", full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)

if (length(nd2_files) == 0) {
  stop(glue("No .nd2 files found in '{cfg$input_dir}'."))
}

# ── Exclude single-image files (e.g. "_S<n>" suffix — no Z-stack) ────────
if (!is.null(cfg$exclude_pattern)) {
  stems      <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(nd2_files))
  is_excluded <- str_detect(stems, cfg$exclude_pattern)
  if (any(is_excluded)) {
    message(glue(
      "Excluding {sum(is_excluded)} file(s) matching exclude_pattern:\n",
      paste(basename(nd2_files[is_excluded]), collapse = "\n")
    ))
  }
  nd2_files <- nd2_files[!is_excluded]
}

if (length(nd2_files) == 0) {
  stop("All .nd2 files were excluded by exclude_pattern.")
}
```

```{r parse-filenames}
# ── Parse each filename against cfg$filename_pattern ─────────────────────
parse_nd2_filename <- function(path, pattern) {
  stem  <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path))
  match <- stringr::str_match(stem, pattern)

  if (all(is.na(match))) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # str_match with named groups returns a matrix whose columns are named
  group_names <- colnames(match)
  group_names <- group_names[group_names != "" & !is.na(group_names)]

  vals <- as.list(match[1, group_names])
  names(vals) <- group_names

  vals$file <- path
  vals$stem <- stem
  as_tibble(vals)
}

parsed <- map(nd2_files, parse_nd2_filename, pattern = cfg$filename_pattern)

unmatched <- nd2_files[map_lgl(parsed, is.null)]
if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
  warning(glue(
    "{length(unmatched)} file(s) did not match filename_pattern and will be skipped:\n",
    paste(basename(unmatched), collapse = "\n")
  ))
}

parsed_df <- bind_rows(parsed[!map_lgl(parsed, is.null)])

if (nrow(parsed_df) == 0) {
  stop("No filenames matched the configured filename_pattern. Check cfg$filename_pattern.")
}

# Required columns check
required_cols <- c("biofilmNo", "z")
missing_cols  <- setdiff(required_cols, names(parsed_df))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop(glue(
    "filename_pattern is missing required named group(s): {paste(missing_cols, collapse = ', ')}"
  ))
}
if (!"zoom" %in% names(parsed_df)) {
  parsed_df$zoom <- NA_character_
}

parsed_df <- parsed_df %>%
  mutate(
    z_num    = as.integer(z),
    zoom_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(zoom)),
    has_zoom = !is.na(zoom_num)
  )
```

```{r python-setup}
reticulate::py_require(packages = cfg$py_packages)

# py_require() only *declares* requirements — nothing is actually
# provisioned until Python is initialized. py_config() forces that
# initialization now (via uv) and returns the resolved interpreter path,
# which we then use explicitly in system2() calls below. This guarantees
# nd2_composite.py runs under the same environment reticulate just set up,
# rather than whatever unrelated "python3" happens to be on PATH.
py_exe <- reticulate::py_config()$python
message(glue("Using Python: {py_exe}"))

# ── Fallback: verify each required package actually imports ─────────────
# On older reticulate versions (pre ~1.41), py_require()'s automatic
# per-project environment provisioning isn't available, and reticulate
# silently falls back to whatever Python/venv it finds — which may not
# have these packages installed. This checks each package imports and,
# if not, pip-installs it directly into that same interpreter so the
# rest of the document still works regardless of reticulate version.
py_import_name <- function(pkg) {
  # A handful of PyPI names differ from their importable module name.
  overrides <- c("python-pptx" = "pptx", "Pillow" = "PIL")
  if (pkg %in% names(overrides)) overrides[[pkg]] else pkg
}

for (pkg in cfg$py_packages) {
  mod <- py_import_name(pkg)
  ok  <- tryCatch({ reticulate::py_run_string(glue("import {mod}")); TRUE },
                   error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (!ok) {
    message(glue("'{mod}' not importable under {py_exe} — installing '{pkg}' via pip..."))
    result <- system2(py_exe, c("-m", "pip", "install", "--quiet", pkg),
                       stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
    message(paste(result, collapse = "\n"))
    reticulate::py_run_string(glue("import {mod}"))  # re-check; errors loudly if still missing
  }
}
```

```{r convert-to-tiff}
# ── Run nd2_composite.py on each source file (skips existing outputs
#    unless cfg$force_reconvert is TRUE) ──────────────────────────────────

expected_tiff_path <- function(stem) {
  file.path(tiff_dir, paste0(stem, cfg$py_suffix, ".tiff"))
}

parsed_df <- parsed_df %>% mutate(tiff_path = expected_tiff_path(stem))

to_convert <- parsed_df %>%
  filter(cfg$force_reconvert | !file.exists(tiff_path))

if (nrow(to_convert) > 0) {
  for (f in to_convert$file) {
    args <- c(
      cfg$py_script,
      f,
      "--output", tiff_dir,
      cfg$py_extra_args
    )
    message(glue("Running: {py_exe} {paste(args, collapse = ' ')}"))
    result <- system2(py_exe, args = args, stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
    status <- attr(result, "status")
    message(paste(result, collapse = "\n"))
    if (!is.null(status) && status != 0) {
      warning(glue("nd2_composite.py failed for {basename(f)}:\n{paste(result, collapse = '\n')}"))
    }
  }
}

# nd2_composite.py names output "<parentname>_<stem><suffix>.tiff" when an
# --output dir is given and the source isn't directly under that dir; since
# our sources sit directly in cfg$input_dir this simplifies to "<stem><suffix>.tiff".
# Re-check actual files on disk in case naming differs and fix up tiff_path.
actual_tiffs <- list.files(tiff_dir, pattern = "\\.tiff$", full.names = TRUE)

match_actual_tiff <- function(stem) {
  hit <- actual_tiffs[str_detect(basename(actual_tiffs), fixed(stem))]
  if (length(hit) >= 1) hit[1] else NA_character_
}

parsed_df <- parsed_df %>%
  mutate(tiff_path = map_chr(stem, match_actual_tiff))

missing_tiffs <- parsed_df %>% filter(is.na(tiff_path) | !file.exists(tiff_path))
if (nrow(missing_tiffs) > 0) {
  warning(glue(
    "{nrow(missing_tiffs)} composite TIFF(s) could not be found after conversion:\n",
    paste(missing_tiffs$stem, collapse = "\n")
  ))
}

parsed_df <- parsed_df %>% filter(!is.na(tiff_path), file.exists(tiff_path))
```

```{r convert-to-png}
# ── Convert composite TIFFs to PNG for embedding in the pptx ─────────────
tiff_to_png_path <- function(tiff_path) {
  file.path(png_dir, paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(tiff_path)), ".png"))
}

parsed_df <- parsed_df %>% mutate(png_path = tiff_to_png_path(tiff_path))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(parsed_df))) {
  tp <- parsed_df$tiff_path[i]
  pp <- parsed_df$png_path[i]
  if (!file.exists(pp) || cfg$force_reconvert) {
    img <- magick::image_read(tp)
    magick::image_write(img, path = pp, format = "png")
  }
}
```

```{r pptx-builder}
# ── PPTX builder (python-pptx) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds slides with precisely positioned images and text captions.
# Used instead of Quarto/pandoc's markdown->pptx path, which cannot
# reliably place multiple images side-by-side on one slide, or place any
# image inside a table cell (both were tested and silently drop images).
#
# Run via reticulate::py_run_string() (not a `{python}` chunk) so this
# stays on reticulate's Python bridge throughout — mixing Quarto's
# Jupyter-based `{python}` engine with reticulate's `py$` object bridge
# in the same document is unreliable.

reticulate::py_run_string("
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN


def new_presentation(width_in, height_in):
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width  = Inches(width_in)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(height_in)
    return prs


def add_title_slide(prs, title, subtitle=''):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title Slide
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(layout)
    slide.shapes.title.text = title
    if len(slide.placeholders) > 1:
        slide.placeholders[1].text = subtitle
    return slide


def _blank_slide_with_title(prs, title):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(layout)

    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(
        Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), prs.slide_width - Inches(1.0), Inches(0.8)
    )
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    tf.text = title
    tf.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(28)
    tf.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    return slide


def add_image_row_slide(prs, title, image_paths, image_width_in,
                          top_in=1.4, gap_in=0.25, captions=None):
    '''Places images left-to-right, horizontally centered as a group.
    Optionally adds a caption text box under each image (captions must be
    the same length as image_paths if provided).
    '''
    slide = _blank_slide_with_title(prs, title)

    n = len(image_paths)
    total_width = n * image_width_in + (n - 1) * gap_in
    start_left = (prs.slide_width.inches - total_width) / 2.0

    caption_height_in = 0.4 if captions else 0.0

    for i, img_path in enumerate(image_paths):
        left = Inches(start_left + i * (image_width_in + gap_in))
        pic = slide.shapes.add_picture(
            img_path, left, Inches(top_in), width=Inches(image_width_in)
        )

        if captions:
            cap_top = Inches(top_in) + pic.height + Inches(0.1)
            cap_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(
                left, cap_top, Inches(image_width_in), Inches(caption_height_in)
            )
            tf = cap_box.text_frame
            tf.text = captions[i]
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.font.size = Pt(14)
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

    return slide


def save_presentation(prs, path):
    import os
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path) or '.', exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(path)
")
```

```{r generate-slides}
# ── Build one slide per BiofilmNo (no-zoom set) and one slide per
#    BiofilmNo covering all zoomed images together, Z1-Z3 side by side,
#    each captioned with its own actual zoom level (zoom values may
#    differ across Z positions on the same slide) ─────────────────────

prs <- reticulate::py$new_presentation(cfg$slide_width_in, cfg$slide_height_in)
reticulate::py$add_title_slide(prs, "Microscopy Imaging Presentation", "")

biofilm_ids <- sort(unique(parsed_df$biofilmNo))

for (bn in biofilm_ids) {

  group <- parsed_df %>% filter(biofilmNo == bn)

  # ── No-zoom slide: Z1-Z3 side by side, no captions ─────────────────
  base_group <- group %>% filter(!has_zoom) %>% arrange(z_num)
  if (nrow(base_group) > 0) {
    reticulate::py$add_image_row_slide(
      prs,
      title           = glue("{bn}"),
      image_paths     = as.list(base_group$png_path),
      image_width_in  = cfg$slide_image_width_in
    )
  }

  # ── Zoomed slide: all zoomed images together, one per Z, each
  #    captioned with its own zoom level ─────────────────────────────
  zoom_group <- group %>% filter(has_zoom) %>% arrange(z_num)
  if (nrow(zoom_group) > 0) {
    reticulate::py$add_image_row_slide(
      prs,
      title           = glue("{bn} — zoomed"),
      image_paths     = as.list(zoom_group$png_path),
      image_width_in  = cfg$slide_image_width_in,
      captions        = as.list(glue("x{zoom_group$zoom_num} zoom"))
    )
  }
}

reticulate::py$save_presentation(prs, cfg$pptx_path)
message(glue("Saved presentation: {normalizePath(cfg$pptx_path)}"))
```
